title: Achieve at least 20% mean weight loss with an approved incretin treatment

concept.text: Produce substantial, sustained weight reduction during pharmacological treatment of obesity. Semaglutide established roughly 15% mean loss, and tirzepatide achieved 20.9% at 72 weeks in SURMOUNT-1. Proposed completion test: FDA chronic weight-management approval supported by a randomized phase 3 trial demonstrating at least 20% mean baseline weight reduction at approximately 72 weeks in adults without diabetes, with superiority to placebo under an estimand that includes treatment discontinuation. Test set by: FDA sets approval; SURMOUNT-1 investigators prespecified the trial endpoints and estimands. The 20% boundary is an editorial breakthrough threshold, not an FDA approval requirement. Reported achieved: FDA approved tirzepatide (Zepbound) on 8 November 2023, following SURMOUNT-1; semaglutide (Wegovy) received chronic weight-management approval on 4 June 2021. Overlaps: END-05. Sources given: [FDA Wegovy approval announcement](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USFDA/bulletins/2e2adc7) ; [FDA Zepbound approval announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-new-medication-chronic-weight-management) ; [SURMOUNT-1 primary publication](https://www.darmzentrum-bern.ch/fileadmin/darmzentrum/Education/Journal_Club/2022/JC-22-07-20_NEJM_Tirzepatide_Once_Weekly_for_the_Treatment.pdf).

page.title: Obesity medicine matching the weight loss of bariatric surgery
page.definition: An approved medicine produces mean weight loss of at least 25% of baseline body weight in adults with obesity. That is the loss a 2024 systematic review, reported by the American Society for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery, found maintained for up to 10 years after gastric bypass or sleeve gastrectomy. The mean counts participants who stop treatment.

goal.need: In 2024, 16% of adults worldwide were living with obesity. FDA associates loss of 5–10% of body weight through diet and exercise with reduced cardiovascular risk in adults with obesity or overweight.

figures.caption: Global adults aged 18 years or older, 2024
figures.note: The obesity population is included in the overweight population.

statements.quote: In light of increasing rates of both obesity and overweight in the United States, today’s approval addresses an unmet medical need.
statements.context: FDA's announcement of Zepbound approval on 8 November 2023.

statements.body: European Association for the Study of Obesity, Obesity Management Task Force
statements.quote: A greater (20% or more) weight loss may be considered for those with greater degrees of obesity
statements.context: The passage specifies BMI ≥35 kg/m². BMI is weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared. This is an individual treatment objective without a specified drug or population mean.

completion.title: An approved obesity medicine produces at least 25% mean weight loss in a phase 3 trial.
completion.criterion: A medicine approved by the FDA or the European Commission for chronic weight management produces, at an approved dose, mean weight reduction of at least 25% from baseline at 72 weeks or later in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in adults without type 2 diabetes who have obesity, or overweight with a weight-related complication. The mean counts every randomized participant, including those who stopped treatment (treatment-regimen estimand); a mean among participants who stayed on treatment does not count. The figure is stated in the approved prescribing information or a peer-reviewed report. Surgery and devices do not count.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas. The 25% figure is the weight loss that a systematic review reported by the American Society for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery found maintained for up to 10 years after surgery; population, duration and analysis follow SURMOUNT-1. No regulator or society sets a weight loss at which a medicine matches surgery.
completion.threshold_quote: Metabolic and bariatric surgery procedures gastric bypass and sleeve gastrectomy demonstrated total weight loss of 31.9% and 29.5% one year after surgery, respectively. Weight loss of approximately 25% was maintained for up to 10 years after surgery.
completion.basis: The former test, at least 20% mean loss, sat just under tirzepatide’s 20.9% in SURMOUNT-1 (95% CI 19.9–21.8) and is now milestone m5. The same review puts continued tirzepatide at 22.5%, below surgery. 25% is the lower, long-term surgical figure; the one-year figures are 29.5% and 31.9%. The test does not ask for 10-year durability or for weight to stay off after the medicine is stopped. FDA’s 2025 draft guidance, EMA’s guideline and EASO’s goals set no such figure.

milestones.title: An incretin agonist reduces body weight in obese mice versus vehicle at P<0.05.
milestones.criterion: The published laboratory test compares body weight during chronic treatment of diet-induced obese mice with vehicle, using repeated-measures ANOVA and P<0.05. Coskun et al. reported that tirzepatide passed this test and produced greater weight loss than semaglutide. Starting mouse weight was about 45 g; group sizes were not stated in the accessible main text.
milestones.set_by: Coskun et al., Eli Lilly and collaborators, published preclinical experiment, Figure 3; an experiment-specific test.
milestones.threshold_quote: P < 0.05 using one-way ANOVA repeated measures versus the vehicle

milestones.title: An incretin agonist reduces human body weight versus placebo by day 29 at P<0.05.
milestones.criterion: The phase 1b test compares change in body weight with placebo at day 29, using a mixed model and a 5% significance level. Among 53 participants with type 2 diabetes, tirzepatide titrated to 10 mg produced a placebo-adjusted reduction of 2.62 kg (95% CI 1.45–3.79). Body weight was a secondary pharmacodynamic endpoint.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly's phase 1b proof-of-concept study, reported by Coskun et al., clinical outcomes and Figure 5; written for adults with type 2 diabetes.
milestones.threshold_quote: Statistically significant at 5% significance level compared to placebo

milestones.title: People receiving an incretin agonist reach ≥10% weight loss at 26 weeks in a phase 2 trial.
milestones.criterion: The prespecified secondary endpoint is the proportion of participants losing at least 10% of baseline body weight at 26 weeks in a randomized dose-ranging trial. NCT03131687 randomized 318 adults with type 2 diabetes; 316 received treatment. Frías et al. reported on 4 October 2018 that 6–39% of tirzepatide recipients across doses reached this endpoint, compared with 0% receiving placebo. The protocol specified no minimum responder proportion.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly, NCT03131687, secondary endpoint reported by Frías et al.; written for adults with type 2 diabetes.
milestones.threshold_quote: proportion of patients with at least 5% and 10% bodyweight loss from baseline to 26 weeks.

milestones.title: A phase 3 incretin trial beats placebo for ≥20% weight-loss responses at 72 weeks.
milestones.criterion: SURMOUNT-1's prespecified key secondary test compares tirzepatide 10 mg or 15 mg with placebo for the proportion losing ≥20% of baseline body weight at 72 weeks, with control of type I error. Among 2,539 randomized adults without diabetes, the estimated proportions were 50% with 10 mg (n=636), 57% with 15 mg (n=630), and 3% with placebo (n=643); both comparisons had P<0.001. The coprimary mean-weight-change and ≥5% response endpoints also met superiority tests. Results were published on 4 June 2022.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly, SURMOUNT-1 protocol NCT04184622, described in the SURMOUNT programme design paper; written for adults without diabetes.
milestones.threshold_quote: Key secondary end points include the proportion of participants achieving a body weight reduction ≥10%, ≥15%, or ≥20%

milestones.title: An FDA-approved obesity medicine produces at least 20% mean weight loss at 72 weeks in phase 3.
milestones.criterion: A medicine approved by the FDA for chronic weight management produces, at an approved dose, mean weight reduction of at least 20% from baseline at 72 weeks in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in adults without type 2 diabetes who have obesity, or overweight with a weight-related complication. The mean counts every randomized participant, including those who stopped treatment. This was the entry’s completion test until 15 November 2026. In SURMOUNT-1, 2,539 adults were randomized and tirzepatide 15 mg weekly gave 20.9% (95% CI 19.9–21.8) against 3.1% with placebo; FDA approved Zepbound on 8 November 2023.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas; the former completion test. The 20% figure equals the goal the European Association for the Study of Obesity set in 2015 for individual patients with BMI of 35 kg/m² or more; no body sets it for a trial mean.
milestones.threshold_quote: A greater (20% or more) weight loss may be considered for those with greater degrees of obesity

milestones.title: A phase 3 trial shows at least 25% mean weight loss, counting participants who stopped treatment.
milestones.criterion: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in adults without type 2 diabetes who have obesity, or overweight with a weight-related complication, one dose of a medicine produces mean weight reduction of at least 25% from baseline at 72 weeks or later, counting every randomized participant, including those who stopped treatment (treatment-regimen estimand). Approval is not required. A sponsor’s announcement counts as a claimed result until a peer-reviewed report. A mean of at least 25% only among participants who stayed on treatment (efficacy estimand) is partial.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas; the completion figure without the approval. The 25% figure is from the systematic review reported by the American Society for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery.
milestones.threshold_quote: Weight loss of approximately 25% was maintained for up to 10 years after surgery.

not_found: Coskun et al.'s supplementary DOCX could not be read, leaving the preclinical mouse group sizes unverified.
The full text of the phase 2 Lancet paper was blocked; its endpoints and results were available in the opened PubMed abstract.

results.finding: LY3298176 reduced body weight versus vehicle in diet-induced obese mice (group sizes unstated), P<0.05.
results.detail: Chronic treatment was assessed by repeated-measures ANOVA. Starting weight was about 45 g; weight loss also exceeded semaglutide.
results.quote: Chronic treatment with LY3298176 resulted in a significant dose-dependent decrease in body weight that was more pronounced than that observed with semaglutide

results.finding: In 53 participants with type 2 diabetes, LY3298176 titrated to 10 mg reduced body weight by 2.62 kg versus placebo at day 29.
results.detail: The placebo-adjusted reduction had a 95% CI of 1.45–3.79 kg. Body weight was a secondary pharmacodynamic endpoint analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures at a 5% significance level.
results.quote: doses of 10 mg and 15 mg had a relevant effect in T2DM patients (LSM difference [95% CI]: −2.62 kg [−3.79, −1.45] and −2.07 kg [−3.25, −0.88], respectively.

results.finding: LY3298176: 6–39% achieved ≥10% weight loss at 26 weeks in a phase 2 trial with 318 randomized participants (316 treated).
results.detail: Prespecified secondary endpoint assessed in the modified intention-to-treat on-treatment dataset; 0% of placebo recipients reached the target. No minimum responder proportion was required.
results.quote: At 26 weeks, 14-71% of those treated with LY3298176 achieved the weight loss target of at least 5% (vs 22% with dulaglutide, 0% with placebo) and 6-39% achieved the weight loss target of at least 10% (vs 9% with dulaglutide, 0% with placebo).

results.finding: Tirzepatide 15 mg (n=630; trial N=2,539) produced ≥20% weight loss in 56.7% of participants at 72 weeks.
results.detail: The placebo response was 3.1%; the adjusted difference's 95% CI excluded zero. However, the supplied excerpt does not establish prespecification or type I error control for this endpoint; the relevant table footnotes are missing.

results.finding: Zepbound 15 mg (n=630; trial N=2,539) produced 20.9% mean weight loss at 72 weeks.
results.detail: The FDA label authorizes 15 mg weekly for chronic weight management. Study 1 was randomized, double-blind and placebo-controlled, excluded type 2 diabetes, and reports an intention-to-treat population including all randomized patients.

results.finding: Tirzepatide 15 mg (n=630; trial N=2,539) produced 20.9% mean weight loss at 72 weeks.
results.detail: The reported intention-to-treat mean includes all randomized participants but falls below the required 25% threshold.

results.finding: FDA approved Zepbound (tirzepatide) for chronic weight management; trial sample size and mean weight loss are not reported.
results.detail: Establishes FDA approval on 8 November 2023, but provides no phase 3 weight-loss results, approved dose, or treatment-regimen estimand to establish the ≥20% mean reduction at 72 weeks.
results.quote:
We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective 
on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon 
labeling.

results.finding: CT-388 produced a placebo-adjusted weight change of −7.5% at day 29 in cohort 8 of a 24-participant multiple-dose study.
results.detail: Mixed-effects analyses were used, but no formal hypothesis testing was performed and no P values were reported. Participants had overweight or obesity without diabetes; this was not the specified 53-participant tirzepatide trial.
results.quote: percent change from baseline in body weight at day 29 among participants treated with CT-388 was −4.1% (−6.37, −1.80) in cohort 6, −5.6% (−7.93, −3.28) in cohort 7, and −7.5% (−9.81, −5.25) in cohort 8.

results.finding: In a randomized phase 2 trial of orforglipron (272 adults), up to 71% of recipients lost at least 10% of baseline body weight by week 26.
results.detail: The dose-ranging trial prespecified ≥10% weight loss at week 26 as a secondary endpoint. It studied adults without diabetes (NCT05051579), rather than the cited tirzepatide trial. Efficacy analyses excluded data after permanent treatment discontinuation and imputed missing outcomes.
results.quote:

to 71% of participants who received orforglip -
ron.

results.finding: SURMOUNT-1 (N=2,539): 57% receiving tirzepatide 15 mg achieved ≥20% weight loss at 72 weeks.
results.detail: Responses were 50% with 10 mg (n=636), 57% with 15 mg (n=630), and 3% with placebo (n=643). Both prespecified comparisons and both coprimary endpoints met superiority (P<0.001), with type I error control. The treatment-regimen estimand included discontinuations. Adults without diabetes; published June 4, 2022.
results.quote:
50% (95% CI, 46 to 54) and 57% (95% CI, 53 to 61) of participants in the 
10-mg and 15-mg groups had a reduction in body weight of 20% or more, as 
compared with 3% (95% CI, 1 to 5) in the placebo group

results.finding: Retatrutide 12 mg produced 25.0% mean weight loss at 80 weeks in TRIUMPH-1 (2,339 randomized participants; 584 assigned to 12 mg).
results.detail: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in eligible adults without diabetes. The treatment-regimen estimand included all randomized participants regardless of treatment discontinuation or use of prohibited weight-management treatments.
